title: Chocolate Hearts Box

adjustment.analysis: No drivers are active: no events, promotions, or price changes. The baseline already reflects the seasonal trend (back-to-school season) and recent fluctuations. Past promotions show no persistent uplift (noise-adjusted x1.0), and the post-promotion week effect is also noise-adjusted to x1.0. The classical uplift model correctly identifies no signal. The product’s ordinary week volatility (±63%) makes small deviations unreliable. The baseline’s median (8.3) is already well-calibrated.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-63% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
